reconfigures

/ree-kuhn-FIG-yerz/ - the stress falls on FIG · verb

What It Means

Reconfigures means arranges into a new form or layout.

One switch reconfigures the drone's rotors, folding the wide camera platform into a narrow racing frame.

Worked Example

On tournament weekends the arcade's manager reconfigures the floor: racing pods unbolt and roll to the walls, ticket counters pivot, and by morning the same footprint holds forty folding chairs, a stage, and a scoreboard. Monday it all rolls back. Nothing is bought and nothing is thrown away; the room simply takes a new shape.

Reconfigures is the exact word for what he does, because it means arranges into a new form or layout — the parts stay, the pattern changes. Rearranges covers a casual shuffle of furniture; reconfigures suggests a system with planned layouts, snapped from one into another.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

rearranges: Rearranges is the everyday word for moving the same pieces into a new order — furniture shoved around a living room until it feels right. Reconfigures suggests a system with planned layouts behind it: cabins, consoles, software, floor plans snapped from one designed arrangement into another.

reshuffles: Reshuffles means quick, informal changes of order — a deck cut again, a batting lineup juggled, a schedule swapped about, often only for now. Reconfigures is the engineered version: the same parts locked deliberately into a planned new layout, a whole system changing shape on purpose.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

freezes: locks the current layout exactly where it stands

sets in stone: makes an arrangement permanent on purpose

Where it sits · how much of the old form changes — adjusts → reconfigures → rebuilds

adjusts vs. reconfigures: Adjusts is a far lighter change than reconfigures — one shelf slides, one chair turns, and the room is otherwise itself — while reconfiguring redraws the whole layout at once.

rebuilds vs. reconfigures: Rebuilds goes further than reconfigures — the old form is demolished and new parts are made, where reconfiguring only rearranges the parts already there.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together

Root — figur-

Root — figur-: shape, form (Latin figura)

Suffix — -es

Suffix — -es: he, she, or it does

Put it together

Put it together: Re- (again) + con- (together) + figur- (shape) + -es = shapes it together again. A configuration is how parts stand together; reconfiguring keeps every part and redoes the togetherness — a new layout from the same pieces. Another clean 'again.'

Use the root in a new word: figurine

Use the root in a new word: figurine: A figurine is a little shaped form — the same figur- that reconfiguring rearranges wholesale.

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Reconfigures is precise about one thing: the parts stay, the arrangement changes. Rearranges is the everyday twin; reconfigures suggests a system — cabins, consoles, software, floor plans — snapped into a planned new layout. Unit-mates to keep straight: recalibrated corrects an instrument's accuracy without moving anything, and refurbish cleans and repairs without redesigning. Only reconfigures redraws the map.
